title: To Develop Without Becoming an Individual an Approach to the Appeal of “Collective Personal Development Kits” From Erich Neumann
abstract: Contemporary individuals increasingly experience generalized disorientation, loss of meaning, and psychological distress—phenomena that empirical research has linked to alienation and meaninglessness. In response, a wide range of cultural, political, spiritual, and pop-psychological proposals have emerged that promise authenticity and development. This article problematizes a paradox at the heart of such proposals: although they claim to foster development, they often culminate in new forms of undifferentiation. The central hypothesis advanced is that these proposals—here termed collective development kits—can be read as deriving their appeal from a uroboric-incestuous dynamic, as conceptualized by Erich Neumann. Drawing on Neumann’s account of primordial unity, development, and the symbol of the uroboros, the article argues that these kits simultaneously activate two constitutive yet opposed human inclinations: the drive toward personal development and the temptation to regress into undifferentiated unity. Rather than fostering human flourishing and development, they short-circuit its demands and dissolve singularity into pseudo-collective unities. The article proceeds by (I) reconstructing Neumann’s theory of primordial unity and symbolic mediation, (II) analyzing the regressive logic of uroboric incest, and (III) applying this framework to explain the contemporary appeal and psychological risks of collective development kits.
